headline: A sharply colder, sunny stretch Tuesday and Wednesday gives way to a strong Thanksgiving storm that will likely bring 1–2 inches of rain, east-northeast gusts of 35–45 mph (possibly over 50 mph at the coast) and widespread coastal flooding.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A cold front crossed the area Monday afternoon, ending a run of unusually mild afternoons and bringing in much colder air. Winds have shifted to the northwest with a few gusts near 23 mph this afternoon, then ease Monday night under dry skies. For reference, Monday's record highs are 72 at Central Park (1931), 74 at Newark, 70 at LaGuardia and 71 at JFK.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday is sunny but much colder, with highs struggling to reach 50 and most places topping out in the upper 40s, and northwest winds picking up to about 17–29 mph. Tuesday night is the coldest night of the season so far: below freezing outside the New York City metro area, with the city itself dropping into the mid 30s. Wednesday is similar, with winds turning northeast and clouds increasing in the afternoon ahead of a storm approaching from the south.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: An impactful storm is increasingly likely on Thanksgiving, driven by a very strong high over the Northeast squeezing against a deepening low moving up into the Mid-Atlantic: east-northeast winds of 15–25 mph develop by late Thursday morning, with gusts peaking at 35–45 mph Thursday afternoon and evening, possibly over 50 mph along the coast for a time, and wind advisories may eventually be needed. A period of steady moderate, locally heavy rain comes Thursday into Thursday night, starting as early as Thursday morning or as late as early Thursday evening because the main computer models still differ by 6–12 hours; 1–2 inches is expected on average, with localized amounts near 3 inches. A low-end (marginal) risk of excessive rain covers the whole region, but minor flooding in urban and poor-drainage areas is far more likely than flash flooding, and river and stream flooding should be limited because the storm moves through quickly. Friday turns blustery with west winds gusting about 29–40 mph as the storm departs, and Saturday stays breezy with west gusts of about 23–35 mph.

coast: Coastal flooding is growing more likely, with a full moon on Tuesday the 24th and king tides this week: many locations need less than a foot of extra water to reach minor flooding. Localized minor coastal flooding is possible with Wednesday morning's high tide, then the forecast supports widespread minor to moderate flooding from Thursday morning through Friday morning. Localized major flooding is possible in the most vulnerable spots along the South Shore back bays and western Great South Bay, and at a few northeast New Jersey spots such as Kearny Point and the Hackensack River; some guidance has raised the odds of localized major flooding, and how fast and how far inland the storm tracks will decide how long the flood-driving east-northeast winds last before turning south-southwest. Beach flooding, erosion and overwash are all possible, though overwash looks isolated for now. On the water, Small Craft Advisories run until 1 AM Tuesday for Long Island Sound east of the Connecticut River and until 1 PM Tuesday for the ocean waters, with seas near 5 feet and gusts near 29 mph (25 knots) Tuesday afternoon before conditions ease Tuesday evening. After a lull into Wednesday, winds ramp up Wednesday night: gale-force winds (about 39–54 mph) are likely on all waters, with possible storm-force winds on the ocean Thursday into Thursday evening, and waves up to 15–20 feet on the ocean (occasionally 20–25 feet out east), 7–10 feet on Long Island Sound and around 10 feet on western Block Island Sound east of Orient Point; gales may continue into Friday.
watch_for: Widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding Thursday morning through Friday morning, possibly major in the most vulnerable spots, helped by king tides and the full moon.
Thanksgiving wind gusts of 35–45 mph, possibly over 50 mph along the coast, strongest Thursday afternoon and evening.
Rain timing on Thanksgiving (morning versus evening) and totals of 1–2 inches, locally near 3.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the sharply colder, dry Tuesday and Wednesday, and increasingly confident in an impactful Thanksgiving storm, though rain timing, wind strength and how severe the coastal flooding gets still vary among the models several days out.
